case_title: ABDUL NAWAZ v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL
trial_court_outcome: Convicted u/s 302 IPC and sentenced to imprisonment for life
high_court_outcome: Upheld conviction and sentence of life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder punishable u/s 304(1) of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused and his companions were involved in a scuffle with a deceased Head Constable while attempting to recover a dinghy. The accused picked up a dao, inflicted a blow on the deceased's head, and pushed him into the sea. The deceased's body was later recovered from the sea. The prosecution case was based on the testimony of witnesses who described the sequence of events, including the use of a dao and the pushing of the deceased into the sea. The trial court convicted the accused of murder, but the High Court and the Supreme Court re-evaluated the evidence and found that the act of pushing the deceased into the sea, combined with the head injury, constituted culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction under Section 304(1) of the IPC and sentenced the accused to eight years of imprisonment.
